implementationSummary: CI-WAVE-3 (#661): the `changes` job in .github/workflows/pr.yml no longer force-sets every domain output true for wave-tier pushes. A new 'Resolve wave-push diff range' step (wave tier only) classifies github.event.before: zero/missing (new branch) or unresolvable via `git cat-file -e` (force-pushed branch whose prior tip this checkout can't see) sets fallback=true; otherwise fallback=false. A second dorny/paths-filter run (id: filter-wave, gated on tier=='wave' && fallback=='false') diffs base: github.event.before -> ref: github.event.after using the identical filter definitions as the issue-tier step (shared via a YAML anchor, not duplicated). The 'Set path-filter outputs' step now forces all-true only for tier=='main' (wave->main stays the full, path-aware checkpoint, unchanged) or for the documented wave-tier fallback; a real wave-tier push reads steps.filter-wave's actual diff outputs. Because integration-tests, architecture-gates, and cross-module-contracts already gate on needs.changes.outputs.backend=='true' (and frontend/demo-frontend on dashboard/demo), they become domain-proportional automatically once `changes` stops forcing true -- no changes needed to those job conditions. gitleaks and status-check's tier-aware classification remain fully unconditional (untouched), so cheap docs/agent-only wave pushes never bypass them. merge_group's live Partner policy, issue-tier path filtering, and the main-tier artifact-gate (#660) are byte-for-byte unchanged -- only the `changes` job gained the two new steps and a rewritten set-outputs branch. Extended tests/unit/test_three_tier_ci_contract.py (not a new file) with 7 tests: one guarding the force-true branch is narrowed, one each for backend-only and frontend/demo-only domain matching via the real filter-wave step, one for agent/docs-only staying cheap without bypassing gitleaks, one asserting the before-SHA fallback is documented in-workflow, one that extracts and actually executes the 'Resolve wave-push diff range' bash script against real git repos (zero SHA, empty SHA, garbage SHA, and a real resolvable SHA) to verify fallback=true/false behaviorally rather than just textually, and one confirming wave->main/merge_group are untouched.
assumptions: The 'documented bounded fallback' required by the acceptance criteria for a zero/unresolvable before SHA is to run every domain for that one wave push (matching the pre-CI-WAVE-3 all-true behavior) rather than failing the run outright -- this matches the release-evidence-plan's rollbackAssertion ('wave pushes keep running every domain ... slower but never less safe') and its before-sha-edge-fails-safe journey assertion that the fallback direction must not silently skip checks.

dorny/paths-filter@v4 accepts explicit `base`/`ref` SHA inputs for a push-event run (as it already does implicitly via github.event.before for unconfigured push runs); the wave-tier step passes them explicitly so the diff range is auditable in the workflow file rather than left to the action's push-event default.

Jobs that already condition on needs.changes.outputs.<domain> (integration-tests, architecture-gates, cross-module-contracts, frontend, demo-frontend) did not need their own `if:` changed -- they become domain-proportional purely because the `changes` job's outputs are no longer forced true at wave tier. dependency-validation was left ungated by domain, since it validates the whole pip/pnpm/npm dependency graph as a unit and has no single-domain output to key off.
risks: actionlint validates YAML/expression syntax only, not live GitHub Actions execution; the wave-tier dorny/paths-filter step's explicit base/ref SHA inputs and the git cat-file resolvability check could not be exercised against an actual GitHub push event in this environment. The before-SHA resolution bash was independently verified by extracting and executing the exact script from pr.yml against real local git repos (zero SHA, empty SHA, garbage SHA, valid SHA) in test_wave_push_before_sha_resolution_script_behaves_correctly, which passed for all four cases.

The YAML anchor (&domain-path-filters / *domain-path-filters) reusing the filters block between the issue-tier and wave-tier paths-filter steps is standard YAML and actionlint parses it cleanly, but has not been confirmed against GitHub's own workflow-file parser in a live run.

No live GitHub Actions run of a domain-matched wave push (backend-only, frontend/demo-only, agent/docs-only) was performed -- verification is limited to the static/behavioral contract tests and actionlint per the release-evidence-plan's candidateVerificationJourney, which explicitly scopes this slice to no deployed candidate.
